around.headline: Bengaluru techie's ₹1.75 lakh 'grew' to a fake ₹9.75 lakh in a trading app — then it vanished
around.summary: A Bengaluru techie was lured into a fake trading app that showed inflated returns, watching a ₹1.75 lakh deposit balloon to a fake ₹9.75 lakh before the money disappeared; police separately busted a wider fraud network using fake apps, mule accounts and a crypto trail, per Deccan Herald and The Indian Express. Never invest more because an app's dashboard shows rising profits — verify any broker or trading platform against SEBI's official registration list first.

around.headline: Train mows down student wearing earphones; locals demand a footbridge
around.summary: A student was killed after being hit by a train while wearing earphones near a crossing, prompting locals to demand a footbridge at the spot, per The Times of India. Skip earphones (or keep one ear free) whenever you're near an unmanned or informal rail crossing.

around.headline: Overnight rain snarls traffic; IMD warns of more rain and gusty winds for three days
around.summary: Rain slowed movement on several Bengaluru roads overnight and into Tuesday morning, and the IMD has forecast more rain, thunderstorms and gusty winds over the next three days, per The Hindu, Bangalore Mirror and Deccan Herald. Build in extra travel time and avoid known waterlogging stretches through the week.
around.source: The Hindu, Bangalore Mirror, Deccan Herald

around.headline: South Bengaluru to face Cauvery water supply disruption today
around.summary: Parts of South Bengaluru will see a Cauvery water supply disruption today for maintenance work, per The Times of India. If you're in the affected area, store water in advance to avoid a dry tap later in the day.

around.headline: Karnataka High Court stays deferment of revised minimum wages
around.summary: The Karnataka High Court has stayed the state government's move to defer implementation of revised minimum wages, per The Times of India. If you're a wage-earner, this keeps the higher, revised rate in effect for now rather than pushing it further out.

around.headline: Supreme Court's Tata-Mistry verdict settles who controls Tata Sons' votes
around.summary: A Supreme Court verdict in the long-running Tata-Mistry dispute has clarified that Tata Trusts retain the deciding voting rights in Tata Sons, closing a key chapter of the boardroom battle that began with Cyrus Mistry's 2016 ouster, per The Indian Express. It matters beyond the two families — Tata Group employs and touches millions of Indians through its companies, from Tata Motors to TCS.

street_smart.title: A WhatsApp group full of confident-sounding traders keeps posting screenshots of huge daily profits from a new 'trading app.' You join, deposit ₹20,000, and within a week the app's dashboard shows it's grown to ₹35,000. What do you do next?
street_smart.based_on: Real case reported today: a Bengaluru techie deposited ₹1.75 lakh into a fake trading app that showed the balance inflating to ₹9.75 lakh before the money vanished; Bengaluru police this week uncovered a wider fraud network built on fake apps, mule bank accounts and a crypto cash-out trail.
street_smart.situation: The dashboard numbers look real and climbing, other group members keep posting their own 'proof', and the app is nudging you to add more funds to 'compound your returns' before the next payout cycle closes.

choices.text: Look up the app or broker's registration on SEBI's official intermediary list (or SEBI SCORES) before putting in another rupee, and stop if it isn't listed.
choices.feedback: Correct. Any legitimate stockbroker or trading platform in India must be SEBI-registered, and SEBI publishes the full list for anyone to check. Scam apps never appear on it — they only exist inside the app itself, disconnected from any real exchange.

choices.text: See the balance climbing and deposit more money right away to 'compound' the gains before the payout window closes.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. Inflating an in-app balance and creating urgency to deposit more is the core mechanism of a 'pig-butchering' investment scam — the numbers you see are just a display the scammer controls, and the moment you try to withdraw the full amount, the account gets frozen, blocked, or a fake 'tax' fee is demanded.

choices.text: Ask the other members of the WhatsApp group whether the app has paid them out, and go by what they say.
choices.feedback: Risky. Scam groups are often seeded with the scammer's own accounts or paid actors posting fake screenshots to build social proof — a stranger's word in the same group you were recruited into isn't independent verification.

choices.text: Withdraw a small amount first, and treat a successful payout as proof the platform is safe to invest more in.
choices.feedback: Risky. Scammers frequently allow small early withdrawals on purpose, precisely so victims relax and deposit larger sums afterward. Passing a small withdrawal test doesn't rule out a scam — only independent registration checks do.

takeaways: Before investing in any app or broker, check its registration on SEBI's official site (sebi.gov.in) or the SEBI SCORES portal at scores.sebi.gov.in — a real platform will always be listed.
A rising in-app balance or a successful small withdrawal is not proof of legitimacy — both are tactics scammers use deliberately to build trust before the big theft.

If you've already sent money to a suspicious app, report it immediately to the National Cybercrime Helpline (1930) or cybercrime.gov.in — funds are only recoverable within the first few hours before they're moved through mule accounts.

quiz.question: A Bengaluru techie's investment was inflated inside a fake trading app this week — from ₹1.75 lakh to what fake balance, before the money vanished?
quiz.why: Police found the scam relied on a wider network of fake apps, mule bank accounts and a crypto cash-out trail — a pattern known as a 'pig-butchering' scam, where fabricated profits build trust before the victim's money is moved beyond recovery.

quiz.question: What did the Karnataka High Court stay this week, directly affecting wage-earners in the state?
options: The state's deferment of revised minimum wages
quiz.why: Minimum wages in Karnataka are revised periodically based on the cost of living index, and employers are legally required to pay at least the notified rate for each category of work.

quiz.question: The Supreme Court's verdict this week in the long-running Tata-Mistry dispute confirmed that deciding voting rights over Tata Sons rest with whom?
quiz.why: The dispute traces back to Cyrus Mistry's abrupt removal as Tata Sons chairman in 2016, which triggered years of litigation over control of India's largest business conglomerate.

quiz.question: Which constitutional body is responsible for conducting elections and preparing electoral rolls across India?
quiz.why: The Election Commission of India is an independent constitutional authority established under Article 324, tasked with ensuring free and fair elections at every level of government.

quiz.question: Which regulator maintains the official public list of registered stockbrokers and trading platforms in India — the exact list you'd check before trusting a new 'trading app'?
options: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority (IRDAI)
quiz.why: SEBI's SCORES portal (scores.sebi.gov.in) also lets investors file and track complaints against any registered market intermediary, not just look them up.
